title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
pattern: Preorder with markers for empty spots
statement: Design `serialize`, which turns a binary tree into a string, and `deserialize`, which rebuilds exactly the same tree from that string.

example.why: Writing None for every empty spot records the shape, so the string can be read back without guessing.

idea: A plain list of values is not enough — many different trees contain the same values. The **shape** has to be stored too.
Write the tree in preorder (node, then left subtree, then right subtree) and write `None` for every empty spot. With those markers the text describes exactly one tree.
To rebuild, read the tokens in the same order: a value creates a node and is followed by its left subtree and then its right subtree; a `None` means *nothing here*.

complexity.timeWhy: Each node (and each empty spot) is written once and read once; the tokens are joined in a single pass.
complexity.spaceWhy: The string and the token list are proportional to the size of the tree.
